question: What protection is stated for a person even in the extreme case of being bitten by great serpents?
premises: Poison does not enter the body.
This holds even if one has been bitten.
The biting is specified as done by great serpents.
inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
uncertainties: Basis of protection not stated in this verse
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
